care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

To qualify for Child Benefit in the UK, you need to be "responsible" for a child. This usually means either:
1. You live with the child, OR
2. You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent) towards looking after them - for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money

Since Alex doesn't live with you and you're not currently contributing financially to their upkeep, you don't meet the criteria for being responsible for Alex under the Child Benefit rules.

There is normally an 8-week grace period after a child goes to live with someone else, but since it's been more than 8 weeks since Alex moved to live with your ex-partner, this grace period has expired.

**Important note:** Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so it's likely that your ex-partner may be claiming (or could claim) Child Benefit for Alex if they are living with and/or supporting them.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex comes back to live with you, or if you start making regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep - you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit at that point.
